narrative.overview:
Every page is a boxed-software manual lying open at one of its divisions. The page ground is that division's divider board, printed in one full hue with a fine paper grain; the reading matter sits on a milk-acetate leaf hinged over it, punched along its bound edge; a stepped rail of colored tabs runs down the fore edge so the reader can see the whole volume and where they are in it. The system is physical and literal: if a device would not exist in a printed, ring-bound manual (a glowing card, a floating action button, a run button), it does not exist here.

The voice is an engineer's reference, not a product site. Density is generous but disciplined: one long measure of serif text per section, heads hanging in a margin column, tables and figures allowed to run wide. Color is structural, never decorative: a hue tells you which Part you are in, and one reserved red tells you that a stated analogy is being corrected. The course explicitly refuses two looks: the docs-site sidebar with a link tree, and the dark AI-console page.

Everything ships as flat HTML files opened from disk. Fonts, the stylesheet, and figures are local; nothing on a page executes. Practice happens in VS Code and the terminal, and the components are built to send the reader there.
keyCharacteristics: Full-hue Part board as the page ground, set once per page by `data-part` on `<body>`, with a fixed fractal-noise grain over it.
Milk-acetate leaf, faintly tinted toward the board, with a crisp cut edge and three binder punches that show depth.
Fore-edge tab rail: one tab per division, tab length proportional to the division's page count; the current tab extends and is punched.
Three voices: condensed Archivo caps for structure, EB Garamond for prose, JetBrains Mono for machine text and numbering.
Short, hard, down-right paper shadows; square sheets; rounded corners only on tabs and keycaps.
One motion token: a 90ms two-step hinge, used only for state changes on interactive elements.
Vermilion exists only on errata slips.

rules.name: The Board Owns the Hue Rule
rules.body: A page's ground hue is chosen by exactly one attribute, `data-part` on `<body>` (`contents`, `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`), which sets `--board` and `--on-board`. Components that must show another Part's hue (rail tabs, row tabs, division tabs) take it from `data-tab`, never from a hardcoded color.

rules.name: The Errata-Only Vermilion Rule
rules.body: Vermilion appears on `.errata` and nowhere else: not for links, warnings, emphasis, or errors in listings. Its rarity is what makes a correction read as a correction.

rules.name: The Tinted Acetate Rule
rules.body: The leaf is never pure white and never a fixed gray; it always carries 3.5% of the board beneath it. Pure white is reserved for keycaps, the errata slip, and type on the vermilion band.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Archivo condensed caps is the manual's structure (heads, tabs, labels, captions' lead words). EB Garamond is the author speaking. JetBrains Mono is the machine and the numbering system: commands, paths, keys, folios, section and reference numbers. A string never borrows another voice.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Condense heads with `font-stretch`, never with a different family: 62–68% for display, 70–72% for headlines and division tabs, 75% for labels and tabs, 78–80% for titles. Heads are uppercase; body text is never condensed.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Addresses Rule
rules.body: The mono number above a section head (`1.1.1`, `1.1.2`…) and the `p. 1.1` folio are a cross-reference system matched by anchor ids (`s-1-1-1`). They are not decoration. There are no eyebrow or kicker labels: no small category line above a title or head; the running head already says where you are.

rules.name: The Hanging Head Rule
rules.body: Heads live in the margin column and text lives in the body column. Do not center headings, do not put a head inside the text column at section level, and do not let prose exceed 62ch.

rules.name: The Flat Files Rule
rules.body: Every page is a flat HTML file at the project root (`index.html`, `part1-1-mental-model.html`, `part2-3-…html`) that references `assets/` relatively. Firefox's `file://` policy only lets a document load fonts from its own directory or below, so a page in a subfolder would lose its typefaces. No CDN, no build step, no network.

rules.name: The Paper Stack Rule
rules.body: Only physical sheets cast shadows, offsets stay at or under 4px with blur at or under 6px, and shadow never signals state. State is shown by position (a tab slides out), outline, or inversion.

rules.name: The Tab Corner Rule
rules.body: A corner is rounded only if it is the free edge of a tab, a key, or a small inline mark (inline code, an inverted citation marker). Everything that is a sheet stays square.

rules.name: The No Run Button Rule
rules.body: Nothing on a page executes. There are no interactive widgets, run buttons, copy-to-run controls, calculators, or live consoles. Labs point to VS Code and the terminal through procedures, where markers, and listings.

rules.name: The Face-Down Rule
rules.body: A page that is not written yet is shown, not hidden: a hatched, full-hue `aria-disabled` rail tab; a dashed `aria-disabled` page turn; a "not yet written" state on the contents page. Never give an unwritten page an `href`.

rules.name: The Hinge Rule
rules.body: The system has one motion token: a 90ms `steps(2, jump-end)` hinge. It moves tabs on `transform`, drops an opening fold on `transform`, rotates the fold triangle, snaps the page-turn and citation inversions, thickens link underlines on hover, and tints a ruled-table row under the pointer (pointer devices, desktop width only). Nothing fades, eases, or animates layout, nothing moves on scroll or page load, and `prefers-reduced-motion` removes every transition and animation.

dos: Do set `data-part` on `<body>` for every page (`contents`, `1`–`4`) and let it choose the board; use `data-tab` on any component that shows another Part's hue.
Do put every page at the project root as a flat file and reference `assets/css/course.css` relatively; keep fonts in `assets/fonts/`.
Do number sections `P.p.n` (`1.1.1`) with a mono `.sec-num` and matching anchor ids, and match the folio in the running head to the page number.
Do keep the hanging-head grid: a 12.5rem margin column for heads, body text at 62ch, `.wide` only for tables and figures.
Do list every unwritten page as a face-down `aria-disabled` tab or turn without an `href`.
Do send labs to VS Code and the terminal with `.procedure`, `.where`, and `.listing`, and label each listing with its file path or "Terminal".
Do caption tables and figures as "Table N." / "Figure N." in condensed bold caps, and give every SVG figure a `<title>` and full `<desc>`.
Do use only the 90ms two-step hinge for motion, and only to show a state change on an interactive element.
Do put deeper dives, troubleshooting, and references in a `details.fold`; keep core theory unfolded.
donts: Don't make the page, the leaf, or a listing dark; the dark AI-console look is rejected.
Don't add a docs-site sidebar or link tree; navigation is the tab rail, the running head, the contents page, and the page turn.
Don't add eyebrow or kicker labels above titles or heads; section numbers and the running head already locate the reader.
Don't add run buttons, interactive widgets, code runners, or in-browser evaluation.
Don't load fonts, scripts, or styles from a CDN, or put pages in subfolders.
Don't round sheets, cards, or panels; only tabs, keycaps, and inline code are rounded.
Don't use shadows for hover or state, or any shadow larger than the paper-stack offsets.
Don't use fades, easing curves, or layout animation.
